question.problem: What is the last digit in the decimal expansion of ${19}^{19}?$
question.worked_solution:
If $a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n)$ and $c≡d\,(\text{mod}\,n),$ then the following properties hold:

- $ac≡bd\,(\text{mod}\,n)$

- ${a}^{k}≡{b}^{k}\,(\text{mod}\,n)$ for any positive integer $k$

To find the last digit, we need to calculate the following residue:

$$
{19}^{19}\text{ mod }10
$$

First, we note the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}19 & ≡10+9\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡0+9\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡9\, & (\text{mod}\,10)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by the exponentiation property, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{19}^{2} & ≡{9}^{2}\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡81\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡8\cdot 10+1\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡8\cdot 0+1\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡1\, & (\text{mod}\,10)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we decompose ${19}^{19}$ into a product of smaller exponents. 

$$
{19}^{19}={({19}^{2})}^{9}\cdot 19
$$

By applying the multiplicative and exponentiation properties, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{19}^{19} & ≡{({19}^{2})}^{9}\cdot 19\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡(1)^{9}\cdot 9\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡1\cdot 9\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡9\, & (\text{mod}\,10)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{19}^{19}\text{ mod }10=9
$$

which means that the last digit of ${19}^{19}$ is $9.$
